definitions.explanation: A warrior or samurai of the pre-modern era. In modern use, appears in historical contexts, festival names (the Boy's Day {五月人形|ごがつにんぎょう}), and set expressions such as {武者震|むしゃぶる}い (a thrill of anticipation before a challenge).

examples.japanese: {武者|むしゃ}の{鎧|よろい}を{見|み}た。
{息子|むすこ}のために{五月人形|ごがつにんぎょう}の{武者|むしゃ}{人形|にんぎょう}を{飾|かざ}った。
examples.english: We displayed a warrior doll among the Boy's Day figures for our son.

examples.japanese: {大会|たいかい}{前|まえ}は{武者|むしゃ}{震|ぶる}いがして、{逆|ぎゃく}に{力|ちから}が{湧|わ}いてきた。
examples.english: Before the tournament I had a shiver of anticipation, which actually filled me with energy.

notes:
An older word, mainly used in historical and ceremonial contexts. Everyday modern speech uses {侍|さむらい} or {兵士|へいし} instead.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {武者|むしゃ}{人形|にんぎょう}: warrior doll (Boy's Day display)
- {武者|むしゃ}{修行|しゅぎょう}: warrior training; (figurative) honing one's skills through hardship
- {武者|むしゃ}{震|ぶる}い: a thrill of anticipation before a challenge
- {落|お}ち{武者|むしゃ}: a defeated warrior fleeing battle

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {侍|さむらい}: samurai — more common everyday word for a warrior of that class
- {兵士|へいし}: soldier — modern, general term
- {武士|ぶし}: warrior class member — emphasizes social class
